errors.finding: Appointment booking chain (Code_Generator → create_appointment) is not structurally gated: confirmation_number is collected as a User-sourced ConfirmationNumber instead of ToolOutput from conf_code.securityCode.
errors.evidence: create_appointment.inputs[confirmation_number] has source User and type ConfirmationNumber (direction input). Code_Generator output is conf_code with securityCode. Prose in Code_Generator inputInstructions says to pass securityCode immediately, but the type graph allows create_appointment without a prior Code_Generator call.
errors.fix: Add an output-direction alias (e.g., GeneratedConfirmationCode) on conf_code.securityCode and map create_appointment.confirmation_number to source ToolOutput with mapping ["conf_code", "securityCode"]. Remove User collection of confirmation_number.

source.section: Prose ordering instead of type ordering

impact.reliability: Model may invent confirmation numbers, skip Code_Generator, or present codes before create_appointment succeeds despite prose rules.

suggestedTests.description: Book appointment end-to-end; trajectory must include Code_Generator before create_appointment with matching confirmation in response.

trajectory.text: I need an appointment next Tuesday at 10am at the Hartford office for unemployment questions.

errors.finding: Role promises change and cancel appointments, but the tool surface only supports create and lookup—no reschedule, update, or cancel Data Actions.
errors.evidence: role: "help residents schedule, verify, change, and cancel appointments" — tools: create_appointment, check_appt only; no cancel/update tools.
errors.fix: Either narrow the role to schedule and verify (lookup) only, or add backend tools (cancel_appointment, reschedule_appointment) with typed inputs/outputs and wire instructions locally on those tools.

impact.reliability: Residents asking to cancel or change will get improvised answers or failed flows.

errors.finding: Opening behavior in role contains conflicting scripts for call_reason and caller_name (duplicate blocks that disagree on whether to ask "How can I help?").
errors.evidence: Early block: when call_reason provided, do NOT ask "How can I help?". Later block: if caller_name provided, greet by name and ask "How can I assist you today?" without conditioning on call_reason. Third block repeats warm greeting rules.
errors.fix: Collapse opening into one decision tree in start-context configuration or a short role paragraph: (1) greet with name if present, (2) if call_reason present acknowledge and route, else ask how to help, (3) if name missing collect name first. Remove duplicate paragraphs and long worked examples from role.

warnings.finding: Role is excessively long and procedural (multi-paragraph call_reason scripts, examples, repeated greeting rules)—violates instruction locality and adds per-turn token cost.
warnings.evidence: Role exceeds ~1.5k words with embedded dialog examples and duplicates guidelines already in instructions[] (claim lookup, knowledge grounding, resident term).
warnings.fix: Trim role to brand, DOL scope, resident term, high-level capabilities/exclusions, and start-context one-liner; move call_reason/caller_name branching to Architect or a compact start-context instruction block.

warnings.finding: check_appt pushes parallel-array indexing logic to the model instead of returning a single matched appointment record from the data action.
warnings.evidence: outputInstructions instruct: find index where entities_key matches confirmation_number, then read entities_appt_date[index], etc. Output schema exposes seven parallel string arrays.
warnings.fix: Change miked_getappt_generic_v4 to return one object with record_found flag and flat fields (or a single array item); replace array-index outputInstructions with success/no-result templates.

source.section: Tools — raw API payloads / agent logic

impact.reliability: Wrong index or empty arrays causes incorrect appointment details or hallucinated slots.

warnings.finding: Code_Generator exposes static parameters length and characters as required User inputs although type descriptions fix them to 6 and 0123456789.
warnings.evidence: Length description "always 6" but schema default length 5; Characters default "012345679" (missing digit 8). Both inputs source User, required true.
warnings.fix: Hardcode length/charset in the data action; drop agent-facing inputs. Align confirmation length with ConfirmationNumber_1 description (6 digits).

warnings.finding: check_appt description references "repair appointment"—leftover domain wording for DOL labor appointments.
warnings.evidence: description: "Look up a repair appointment using a confirmation number."
warnings.fix: Rewrite to DOL appointment lookup by confirmation number; add inputInstructions for when to use vs create_appointment.

warnings.finding: Global instructions[] duplicate tool-local behavior (claim status summaries, appointment confirmation messaging, tool failure transfer) already covered on Claim Lookup and create_appointment.
warnings.evidence: 15 guidelines including claim lookup steps overlapping Claim Lookup outputInstructions; appointment confirmation rules overlap create_appointment outputInstructions.
warnings.fix: Keep guidelines for cross-cutting grounding, fraud escalation, and privacy; move claim-specific and appointment-specific post-success behavior to respective tool outputInstructions only.

warnings.finding: Custom guardrails read as agent behavior policies rather than customer-input block rules.
warnings.evidence: "do not allow the caller to force a claim payment"; "Do not allow the user to ask personal questions" — not phrased as blocked customer requests.
warnings.fix: Rephrase to input-focused rules (e.g., "Block customer demands to override claim payment decisions or compel payout") and move eligibility/payment policy to role scope + Claim Lookup/KB. Keep SSN rule as collection constraint in tool/types if last-4 is collected.

warnings.finding: Mixed customer/resident terminology across role, guidelines, and tools.
warnings.evidence: Role uses "residents"; several instructions say "customer" (e.g., "ask the customer to verify the claim number").
warnings.fix: Standardize on "resident" per role; search-replace in instructions[] and tool pre-instructions.

warnings.finding: End context OutputData maps only get_output.entities_* index 0, while check_appt returns arrays—handoff may omit the matched appointment when index ≠ 0.
warnings.evidence: OutputData properties map get_output.entities_key.0, entities_appt_date.0, etc.
warnings.fix: After backend returns a single record, map flat fields; or map the struct produced by a narrowed check_appt output type.

warnings.finding: Broad outputInstructions use when: "True" on every outcome path, reducing conditional specificity and stacking redundant instructions each call.
warnings.evidence: create_appointment, check_appt, Claim Lookup, DLI_KB each have multiple Python outputInstructions with when True.
warnings.fix: Consolidate to one success and one failure/no-result instruction per tool; use lambdas on result shape where KB already does.

info.finding: Version drift: ProductionReady v11.0 matches saved v12.0 Draft definition byte-for-byte in Sage—draft does not yet contain fixes for known structural issues.
info.evidence: get_latest_published_version 11.0 ProductionReady and get_latest_saved_version 12.0 Draft returned identical definition payloads during this critique.
info.fix: Use v12.0 (or next version) to land ToolOutput gating, role trim, and check_appt backend shape before TestReady/ProductionReady publish.

info.finding: Baseline capability map for DOL SC12: appointments (create + lookup), unemployment claim status (ServiceNow incident lookup), general DOL FAQ (DLI_KB KnowledgeSetting), escalation/exit events; no reschedule/cancel/payment tools.
info.evidence: Five tools: Code_Generator, create_appointment, check_appt, Claim Lookup, DLI_KB; integrations miked_* data actions + ServiceNow Get Ticket + MikeD_KB_Config.
info.fix: Document this map in lifecycle design-artifact when branching DOL use cases; add tools before expanding role scope.

info.finding: InputData start context correctly uses alias types CallerName and CallReason without required properties.
info.evidence: InputData.properties caller_name, call_reason optional; types CallerName, CallReason documented for VA flow.
info.fix: Keep; pair with simplified opening role once contradictions are resolved.

positives.finding: DLI_KB KnowledgeSetting has a strong when-to-use scope in description and inputInstructions, with empty/non-empty result branching.
positives.evidence: DLI_KB description lists DOL topics; outputInstructions branch on len(result).
positives.fix: Maintain; avoid duplicating KB routing in global guidelines.

positives.finding: Claim Lookup defines acct_not_found error type with defaultInstruction for 404/400—good no-result path.
positives.fix: Keep; ensure role does not contradict verify-and-retry behavior.

positives.finding: Escalation, UserExit, and Guardrails violation events are configured with resident-facing messages.
positives.evidence: events: Guardrails (threshold 3), UserExit, Escalation transfer message.
positives.fix: Pair with guideline-driven escalate on fraud and tool failures.

changeSuggestions.text: Structurally gate create_appointment.confirmation_number to Code_Generator output (ToolOutput mapping on securityCode).
Resolve role scope vs tools: remove change/cancel from role or implement cancel/reschedule data actions.
Unify opening logic for caller_name/call_reason and dedupe verbose role prose.
Refactor check_appt data action to return a single appointment object with record_found; drop array-index instructions.
Hardcode Code_Generator parameters; fix 6-digit charset consistency.
Reframe guardrails as blocked customer inputs; relocate payment policy to role/tools.

summary.prose: DLI_appointment_miked is a capable DOL demo AVA—appointments (create/lookup), ServiceNow claim status, and MikeD KB—but production traffic still runs v11.0 while v12.0 Draft is unchanged. The highest risk is the booking chain: confirmation numbers are not type-gated to Code_Generator, so the model can skip or invent codes despite prose. Role bloat and contradictory opening scripts add first-turn confusion, and the role over-promises change/cancel without tools. check_appt’s parallel-array contract pushes fragile indexing to the LLM. Address structural tool chaining and scope honesty before publishing v12.
topPriorities: Gate create_appointment.confirmation_number via ToolOutput from Code_Generator (ERR-001)
Align role scope with tools—drop change/cancel or add tools (ERR-002)
Fix conflicting call_reason/caller_name opening scripts and trim role (ERR-003, WARN-001)

gaps: No trajectory test for Code_Generator → create_appointment ordering
No claim lookup INC prefix normalization
No guardrail/adversarial prompts for payment forcing
